recipes.name: Oats and Vegetable Uttapam
recipes.health_benefit: Rich in fiber from oats and vegetables, this recipe supports healthy blood sugar levels, aids in managing cholesterol, and provides sustained energy. It contributes to overall cardiovascular health and gut health.
instructions: Dry roast oats lightly for 2-3 minutes, then let cool and grind into a coarse flour.
In a bowl, combine oat flour, curd, water, and salt to form a smooth batter (similar to dosa batter consistency). Let it rest for 10-15 minutes.
Stir in chopped onion, carrot, bell pepper, green chili, ginger, and coriander leaves into the batter.
Heat a non-stick tawa (griddle) and lightly grease it with oil. Pour a ladleful of batter and spread it gently to form a thick uttapam.
Cook on medium heat until golden brown, then flip and cook the other side. Repeat for remaining batter.
Serve hot with a side of plain curd or a light chutney.

recipes.name: Masoor Dal Tadka with Brown Rice
recipes.health_benefit: This meal is a powerhouse of plant-based protein, dietary fiber, and complex carbohydrates. It significantly aids in managing blood sugar (HbA1c, glucose), reducing cholesterol, and promoting digestive health. Brown rice provides sustained energy.
instructions: Wash masoor dal thoroughly and soak for 20 minutes. Cook dal in a pressure cooker with 3 cups of water and a pinch of turmeric until soft (2-3 whistles).
Separately, cook brown rice according to package instructions or in a pressure cooker with 2 cups water for about 15-20 minutes.
For the tadka: Heat ghee/oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds and asafoetida. Once spluttering, add chopped onion and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cook for a minute. Add chopped tomato and cook until soft and mushy.
Stir in turmeric, coriander, and cumin powders. Cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the cooked dal to the tempering. Add water if necessary to achieve desired consistency. Bring to a simmer, add garam masala (if using) and chopped coriander leaves. Cook for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with brown rice and a side of mixed vegetable sabzi.

recipes.name: Grilled Fish Tikka (Air-fried/Baked)
recipes.health_benefit: This recipe provides lean protein and beneficial Omega-3 fatty acids (especially with fish like surmai or salmon), which are crucial for heart health, maintaining healthy HDL levels, and managing triglycerides. Grilling/baking reduces fat content compared to frying.
instructions: Cut fish into 1.5-inch cubes. Wash and pat dry thoroughly.
In a bowl, combine curd, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, red chili powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, garam masala, and salt. Mix well to form a marinade.
Add fish pieces to the marinade, ensuring they are well coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (or up to 2 hours for better flavor).
Preheat air fryer to 180°C (350°F) or oven to 200°C (400°F). Line baking tray with parchment paper or spray air fryer basket with minimal oil.
Arrange marinated fish pieces in a single layer. Brush lightly with oil.
Air fry for 10-12 minutes, flipping halfway, or bake for 15-20 minutes until fish is cooked through and lightly charred. Cooking time may vary based on thickness.
Serve hot, garnished with onion rings and lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Chicken and Spinach Curry (Palak Chicken)
recipes.health_benefit: This curry is an excellent source of lean protein (chicken), iron, and Vitamin A from spinach. It supports healthy hemoglobin levels and overall energy. The use of spices adds antioxidants.
instructions: Blanch spinach in hot water for 2-3 minutes, then immediately transfer to ice water. Drain and blend into a smooth purée.
Heat oil/ghee in a pan. Add chopped onion and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies. Sauté for a minute until fragrant.
Add chicken pieces and cook until they change color and are lightly seared.
Stir in turmeric powder, red chili powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Cook for 2-3 minutes, adding a splash of water if masalas stick.
Add tomato purée and cook until the oil separates from the masala.
Stir in the spinach purée and water. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 10-12 minutes, or until chicken is fully cooked.
Add garam masala and salt, mix well. Cook for another 2-3 minutes.
Serve hot with multigrain roti or brown rice.

recipes.name: Sprouted Moong Dal Salad with Boiled Egg
recipes.health_benefit: This nutrient-dense snack provides excellent plant-based protein from sprouted moong and animal protein from eggs, essential for muscle health and satiety. It is rich in fiber, vitamins, and minerals, supporting digestion and overall vitality, including Vitamin B12.
instructions: Gently steam sprouted moong dal for 5 minutes (optional, to make them slightly softer and easier to digest) or use raw.
In a large mixing bowl, combine sprouted moong dal, chopped boiled eggs, cucumber, tomato, onion, green chili, and coriander leaves.
Add lemon juice, chaat masala, salt, and black pepper.
Toss everything together gently until well combined.
Serve immediately as a refreshing and nutritious snack or light meal.

recipes.name: Methi Chicken with Multigrain Roti
recipes.health_benefit: This dish combines lean protein from chicken with the numerous health benefits of fenugreek leaves (methi), which are known to aid blood sugar control, support digestion, and provide essential vitamins and minerals. Multigrain roti adds complex carbohydrates and fiber.
instructions: For Methi Chicken: Heat oil/ghee in a pan. Add sliced onion and sauté until golden brown. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cook for a minute.
Add chicken pieces and cook until they change color. Stir in turmeric, red chili, coriander, and cumin powders. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add chopped tomato and cook until soft. Stir in whisked yogurt gradually to prevent curdling. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add chopped fenugreek leaves and water. Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes until chicken is cooked through and gravy thickens. Add garam masala and salt. Mix well.
For Multigrain Roti: Mix multigrain flour with a pinch of salt. Add water gradually and knead into a soft, pliable dough. Let it rest for 15 minutes.
Divide dough into equal portions and roll into thin rotis. Cook on a hot tawa until done, applying light pressure and flipping. Serve hot with Methi Chicken.
